identity.title: Depth-Bounds for Neural Networks via the Braid Arrangement

problem.claim: Determine how many hidden layers ReLU networks need to exactly represent all continuous piecewise-linear functions on R^d.

gap.claim: Outside special cases, the best known general lower bound is two hidden layers.

contributions.claim: For braid-fan-compatible networks, proves an Ω(log log d) hidden-layer lower bound for exactly computing the maximum of d numbers.
Gives a combinatorial proof that the same assumption requires three hidden layers to compute the maximum of five numbers.
Shows that a rank-3 maxout layer followed by a rank-2 layer suffices to represent the maximum of seven numbers, so a natural generalized upper bound is not tight.

stated_novelty.claim: The abstract distinguishes a non-constant dimension-dependent lower bound, a combinatorial proof for five inputs, and a tighter maxout construction for seven inputs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an Ω(log log d) lower bound under braid-fan compatibility.
The authors report replacing an earlier excessive computation for the five-number case with a combinatorial proof.
The authors report that two successive maxout layers of ranks 3 and 2 represent the maximum of seven numbers.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames the open depth question for exact representation by ReLU networks.
Notes that special cases are resolved, but the general lower bound remains two hidden layers.
Restricts attention to braid-fan-compatible networks and derives dimension-dependent and finite-case depth lower bounds.
Provides a rank-3-then-rank-2 maxout construction for seven inputs and uses it to challenge tightness of a natural upper-bound generalization.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs an explicit structural assumption (braid-fan compatibility) with both asymptotic and finite-case depth statements.

lessons.interpretation: Making the scope condition explicit helps align a theoretical claim with the class of models to which it applies.
lessons.application: State the architectural or geometric restriction immediately before each depth bound, then separate asymptotic claims from fixed-size results.
lessons.exception: This is less suitable when the intended result is explicitly unrestricted and the restriction would change the main question.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal compatibility definition, proof details, network width or other model constraints.
It does not quantify the prior maxout upper bound or explain the exact sense in which the generalization is not tight.
No broader empirical evaluation or verification details are provided.
